moss_en.stt: There is a game called How to Fish, a boat, a rod, a lot of fish, and almost nobody seems to be fishing. They are slapping each other in the face, gambling the fish money, fishing with a sniper rifle. It costs about $8. Its makers hoped it might sell 200,000 copies. By early October, one analytics firm estimated more than 10 million. Millions of people bought a fishing game. To do everything else, together, why?
